Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{ST}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{TQ}=b,$ $\overset{\to }{QP}=d,$ and $\overset{\to }{TR}=c.$ Find $\overset{\to }{SP}$ in terms of vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$ To denote the corresponding vectors, use $a$, $b,$ $c,$ and $d.$

$\overset{\to }{SP}=$  
 {{field-1}}
worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $S$ to $P$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{SP}=\overset{\to }{ST}+\overset{\to }{TQ}+\overset{\to }{QP}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/07aebf5a6aaa98c9ec5d4e9801dbe7d2cf3ade86573bcd8ee56db375f3e38575.png)

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{ST}=a,\,\overset{\to }{TQ}=b,\,\overset{\to }{QP}=d.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/7c8c193472acbe72979f8a78fe9bd02726ad98c166381434175d0586bb574cb6.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{SP} & =\overset{\to }{ST}+\overset{\to }{TQ}+\overset{\to }{QP} \\  & =a+b+d.\end{aligned}
$$
